title: Customer-managed network governance — lightweight audit & approval PRD (draft)
summary: Lightweight governance pattern for customer-managed VPC onboarding: minimize required audit payloads, provide short-lived approval gates with emergency bypass + post-facto attestation, and a compact telemetry contract that protects customer PII while enabling SRE/audit needs.
problem_statement: Customers with private deployments ask for strong auditability and an approval process for network changes, but many are sensitive to high retention of logs and heavy evidence bundles. We need a pragmatic PRD that enables compliance teams to get necessary proof while keeping onboarding friction low and respecting customer-managed network constraints.
goals: 1) Define a minimal audit bundle that satisfies common SOC/ISO requests. 2) Design an approval gate flow (can be manual or delegated) with TTL and emergency bypass that produces cryptographic receipts. 3) Provide an operator UX and API for customers/operators to integrate into their change workflows. 4) Ensure telemetry is privacy-preserving and configurable by tenant.
non_goals: We are NOT building a full SIEM or replacing customer-side logs; this PRD does not mandate shipping raw packet captures or complete firewall configs. Not building long-term legal hold features in this phase.
personas:
- Platform Ops (Customer): needs minimal evidence to prove change happened and had approval.
- Customer Security/Compliance: needs audit artifacts and retention controls.
- Redwood SRE / Support: needs compact evidence to triage incidents.
- Platform Engineer (Redwood): implements hooks and rollout UX.
success_metrics:
- 80% of pilot customers can complete VPC onboarding with the lightweight evidence bundle.
- Average approval time <= 15 minutes for delegated approvals.
- Number of audit support tickets related to missing evidence decreases by 60% in first quarter.
- Telemetry storage cost for private onboarding features stays < 5% of total private telemetry spend.
requirements:
Functional requirements:
- R1: Provide an API endpoint for 'request_approval' that accepts a change delta, requester identity, justification, and optional attached evidence (hash references preferred).
- R2: Approval flow must support: delegated approvers, role-based approval chains (1-of-2, 2-of-3), timeouts (auto-escalate), and emergency bypass with mandatory post-facto attestation.
- R3: Produce an immutable 'evidence_receipt' token after approval or bypass; token should include change_id, approver(s), timestamp, policy_id, and a signed hash.
- R4: Define compact audit bundle schema (see audit_sample) limited to metadata and proof artifacts; attachments are optional and should be stored customer-side with only content hash stored by Redwood if requested.
- R5: Telemetry export should be configurable per-tenant (sample rate, redaction rules, retention TTL).
- R6: Provide an operator console list/filter for pending approvals, with quick approve/reject and audit trail view.
Non-functional requirements:
- NFR1: Evidence receipts verifiable offline (public-key signature).
- NFR2: Storage retention configurable (30/90/365 days) and default to 90 days.
api_contract:
Sketch of endpoints and fields (informal):
- POST /v1/vpc-changes/request_approval
  body: { change_id, tenant_id, requester: {id, email}, change_summary, policy_id (optional), evidence_hashes: [sha256], intended_effects, rollback_plan }
- POST /v1/vpc-changes/approve
  body: { change_id, approver_id, decision: approve|reject|bypass, notes }
- GET /v1/vpc-changes/{change_id}/receipt -> returns evidence_receipt (signed)
- GET /v1/tenant/{tenant_id}/approvals?status=pending -> list for console
- Webhook: approvals:approved -> POST to tenant URL with receipt payload (configurable)
Notes: Webhook payloads must be signed; receipts include PKI-signed hash and minimal metadata so tenants can archive locally.
audit_sample:
Minimal audit bundle example (compact) -- plain text illustration:
--- audit_bundle_v1 ---
change_id: ch_20251001_0007
tenant_id: tnt-42
requester: asha.patel@redwood.ai
requested_at: 2025-10-01T14:22:03Z
policy_applied: vpc-minimal-evidence-v1
delta_summary: 'Add route 10.1.0.0/16 -> gateway g-12, update egress rule to allow 443 to 203.0.113.9'
evidence_hashes: ["sha256:3a7f...b2c1"]
approvals: [ { approver: liam.chen@acme.com, method: delegated, decision: approve, at: 2025-10-01T14:34:10Z } ]
receipt_signature: "sig_v1:MEUCIQ..."
retention_policy: 90d
notes: 'Customer redacted above rule details per privacy_profile=masked'
--- end ---
Design notes: keep blob sizes small; prefer hashes and pointers. If customer explicitly opts-in we can request attachments (pcap, config diffs) but default is pointers only.
operator_ux:
- Console: single-pane pending approvals, filters by tenant, age, risk-score. Quick actions: approve, reject, request-more-info.
- Mobile: approve with 2-factor if policy requires escalate.
- Audit viewer: show receipt, change diff (if present), and a minimal timeline.
- Templates: predefined policy templates (low/medium/high risk) with default TTLs and approver roles.
privacy_and_security:
- Store only minimal PII in Redwood logs; allow tenant to configure redaction rules (e.g., mask IPs, partial usernames).
- Evidence hashes are safe to store by default.
- For attachments, prefer customer-side storage integrations (S3 presigned URLs) and only store pointers.
- PKI for receipts: use rotating signing keys, publish current public keys to tenant console for offline verification.
- Audit access control: logs accessible only to tenant admins + assigned Redwood SRE roles; all access must be logged.
rollback_and_emergency:
- Emergency bypass: single authorized operator can bypass when 'safety-mode' set to true; flow requires immediate post-facto attestation within 24 hours and escalates to on-call.
- Post-facto attestation must include: reason, screenshots/logs (optional), and a signed receipt. Failure to attest triggers temporary suspensions of bypass privileges for that approver.
integration_notes:
- Integrations: support customer ticketing (JIRA/ServiceNow) correlators, webhook delivery, and SIEM forwarder endpoints (syslog/CEF optional).
- Recommend a lightweight SDK (python/go) to call request_approval and verify receipts locally before applying changes.
- Provide sample terraform module (examples) that ties change lifecycle to request_approval + wait_for_receipt pattern.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pilot with 3 enterprise customers completing onboarding end-to-end with receipts and console UX.
- Receipt verification script returns OK for all pilot receipts (public key verify).
- Telemetry redaction tests: sensitive fields masked per tenant config.
- Approval drift: when automated policy triggers differ from manual approvals, console flags in 95% of observed cases.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (research + prototypes) — 6 weeks: interviews, sketch API, sample SDK.
Phase 1 (pilot) — 8 weeks: implement core endpoints, console list, receipts, PKI, and run 3 pilots.
Phase 2 (general availability) — 4 weeks: harden retention controls, add SIEM exporters and policy templates, docs + runbook.
Notes: prioritize tenants with compliance-driven needs for pilot.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Customers may expect full packet-level evidence; Mitigation: upfront docs and opt-in attachments only.
- Risk: Key management complexity for receipts; Mitigation: rotate keys regularly and publish keys, provide webhook for key rotation events.
- Risk: Storage costs for attachments; Mitigation: default to pointers-only and charge for attachment retention in billing.
open_questions:
- Q1: What are the legal minimums for evidence across our typical customers (finance vs healthcare)? (Action: ask compliance)
- Q2: Should default retention be 90d or 365d for enterprise? Trade-offs: cost vs auditability.
- Q3: Emergency bypass footprint — should bypass generate a special immutable flag visible to auditors?
- Q4: Which fields must be encrypted at rest by Redwood vs left to tenant-managed storage?
next_steps:
- Schedule interviews with 5 SOC/compliance contacts by 2025-10-15.
- Proto: spin up minimal API and receipt signer, demo to internal SRE by 2025-10-22.
- Draft docs for tenant redaction rules and SDK examples.
- Create JIRA epic NETOPS-802 and link PRs.
